To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) automated segmentation of nuclei and glands is a key step in accurate grading of prostate and cancer histopathology images, and (b) the proposed automated segmentation algorithm is capable of achieving accuracies that are comparable to those obtained by manual detection and segmentation.

(i) the proposed glandular and nuclear detection and segmentation algorithm is effective in extracting morphological and nuclear characteristics for automated cancer grading, (ii) the accuracy of the grading and discrimination results obtained via the proposed algorithm is similar to the accuracy of grading and discrimination results that are obtained manually, and (iii) the proposed algorithm can potentially be utilized in clinical practice to reduce the time and effort required to grade cancerous and benign histopathology specimens.
our gland and nuclei segmentation algorithm can be used to improve the accuracy of automated cancer grading and benign versus cancer discrimination.

the development of a robust and accurate automated system for detection and segmentation of nuclei and glands in prostate and breast cancer images.

developing an automated methodology for detection and segmentation of histological structures of interest, and utilizing the information extracted from the segmented objects to improve the accuracy of automated cancer grading and cancer vs. benign discrimination.
the development and validation of automated methods for the extraction of morphological and textural information from histology images for the purpose of cancer diagnosis and grading.
